gold_diagnosis: Extranodal natural killer/T-cell lymphoma nasal type

1: On examination, the left calf had ill-defined, warm, confluent erythema, edema, and tender induration.
He was started on intravenous ceftriaxone for presumed cellulitis and pyomyositis but did not improve.
2: CT and MRI of the leg revealed gastrocnemius myositis, extensive subcutaneous and superficial myofascial edema, and popliteal lymphadenopathy without evident lymphatic obstruction.
He was started on intravenous ceftriaxone for presumed cellulitis and pyomyositis but did not improve.
3: Six months earlier, incidentally noted bilateral adrenal and periaortic retroperitoneal masses were not further evaluated.
Laboratory studies showed mild lymphocytopenia, moderate anemia, elevated creatine kinase, elevated aldolase, and elevated lactate dehydrogenase; peripheral-blood flow cytometry was unremarkable.
